articles.title: Kamaratsi of Evia – Sprites
articles.author: Τίτος Γιοχαλάς
articles.excerpt: Folk belief from Kamari in Evia about Nereids and sprites that haunt the Kamaratsi river.

image.alt: Image of the Kamaratsi river in Evia

content.value: If we pass through the Kamaratsi, there are Nereids and they will take us. The Kamaratsi is a river. And if we cross the river, there are sprites and we fear they will take us. We make the sign of the cross, we recite the "Creed", we say the "Our Father" so that the Nereids will not take us. They take away our speech, they leave us crippled, they mark us.

articles.title: The Sprite at the Mill – Zakynthos
articles.author: Νικόλαος Γ. Πολίτης
articles.excerpt: Traditional narrative about confronting a sprite at a mill in Zakynthos with ritual protection

content.value: A man from Romiri went to the mill with wheat and was returning with the flour. He placed the two sacks of flour on both sides of the pack animal and sat in the middle himself.

A sprite saw the loaded pack animal but did not see the peasant seated behind, and marveled, saying: "One side loaded, and the other too, and the top load as well! And the rogue must be somewhere behind!" The sprite thought the peasant had stayed behind and the pack animal was making its way to the village on its own.

The sprite turned back to find the peasant, could not see him, went back to the pack animal and said the same things again. The poor peasant, out of fear at seeing the sprite and hearing its words, crouched down even lower.

He then reached home. The sprite became furious at having been fooled and wanted to seize him. But from the cries, his wife understood that the sprites were tormenting her husband, and she came out with incense and other sacred things, and so the sprite became a wretched creature and fled.

articles.title: The Devetsikas of Lidoriki
articles.author: Δημ Λουκόπουλος
articles.excerpt: Folkloric record of the Devetsikas, a sprite that appears as various animals and brings destruction to flocks. This tradition was recorded in Lidoriki and the surrounding pastoral settlements of Fokida.

content.value: The Devetsikas, according to many prevailing beliefs in Lidoriki and the surrounding pastoral settlements, is a sprite that appears in the form of various animals among the sheep and brings destruction.
